purpose: Formal model of cognitive-space exhaustion, frustration, reflection, orthogonal transition, and the emergence of a new differentiation regime.

actualization_mode.description: Current regime through which distinctions become actualized.

accessible_directions.description: Set of currently accessible productive directions of differentiation.

normal_orientation.description: Current orientation of the process relative to its accessible differentiation space.

productive_distinctions.description: Distinctions that generate further accessible distinctions within C_k.

exhaustion.description: Contentual exhaustion of the current differentiation regime, not merely local failure.
condition: the process approaches an invariant regime

formal_signature.interpretation: The current mode increasingly loses productive differentiation and approaches invariance.

distinction_from_local_failure.local_failure: Failure of a particular operation, carrier, branch, or attempt.
distinction_from_local_failure.cognitive_space_exhaustion: Loss of productive differentiation within the current regime itself.

frustration.description: Functional process state produced by exhaustion of the current mode.
frustration.definition: Necessity of continuation under inability to continue productively in the current mode.
role: permit transition to another actualization regime

reflection.description: Process-level recognition that the limitation belongs to the current mode of differentiation rather than merely to a local state.

orthogonal_transition.description: Transition from an exhausted differentiation regime into a structurally continuous but non-identical regime in which further distinctions become possible.
requirements: do not merely repeat exhausted content
change the conditions of further differentiation

mechanism_independence.description: The definition of orthogonal transition does not prescribe a unique mechanism of realization.
mechanism_independence.principle: OT is a structural transition; its concrete realization remains an open variable.

transition_mechanisms.description: Candidate mechanisms through which an orthogonal transition may be realized. No mechanism listed here is constitutive of OT.

candidates.name: scale_transition
candidates.description: Change in the scale or regime at which distinctions are actualized.

candidates.name: compensatory_multiplication
candidates.description: Increase in the number of local actualization nodes that compensates for a change in scale or regime.

candidates.name: structural_reconfiguration
candidates.description: Reorganization of relations while retaining some or all underlying elements.

candidates.name: carrier_transition
candidates.description: Change of the carrier through which the process is actualized.

candidates.name: interaction_regime_transition
candidates.description: Change in the regime of interaction among existing process elements.

candidates.name: representation_space_transition
candidates.description: Change in the representational conditions under which distinctions can be generated.

candidates.name: composition_decomposition_transition
candidates.description: Change in the granularity or organization of process units.

candidates.name: unknown_emergent_mechanism
candidates.description: A mechanism not represented by the current ontology.

scale_transition.description: One possible mechanism of orthogonal transition involving a change in the scale or regime of actualization.
scale_transition.constraint: A scale change qualifies as an orthogonal mechanism only if it changes the space of subsequently accessible distinctions.

compensatory_multiplication.description: One possible mechanism in which a transition of scale or regime is accompanied by multiplication of local actualization nodes.
compensatory_multiplication.hypothesis: A change in actualization regime may be compensated by an increase in the number of local actualization nodes.

node_interaction.description: Interactions among local nodes may generate distinctions unavailable to an isolated node.

generation.description: C_k+1 results from an orthogonal transition whose concrete realization may involve one or more candidate mechanisms.

new_capability.description: The defining property of C_k+1 is not a specific physical or computational structure but the restoration or expansion of productive differentiation.

emergent_distinctions.description: Distinctions that become accessible only after the transition to a new regime.
emergent_distinctions.criterion: A distinction is relevant to the transition when it was structurally inaccessible or unavailable under the exhausted regime.
emergent_distinctions.non_reduction: Emergent distinctions need not be reducible to a simple repetition of distinctions available in C_k.

object_formation.description: A candidate ontological interpretation in which object-like entities are temporary stable regimes generated by relations among actualizations.

force_formation.description: A candidate ontological interpretation in which force-like phenomena arise as relations among local actualizations.

creative_transition.description: A productive transition changes the conditions under which subsequent distinctions can be generated.
creative_transition.criterion: A transition is productively creative when it expands the space of subsequent distinctions.

invariants: No candidate mechanism is constitutive of OT
Orthogonal Transition changes conditions of further differentiation
Process Continuity does not require carrier identity
New regime preserves structural continuity without preserving content identity
